chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah bin al-Mughira, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you enter the mosque, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family); and when you exit, do that (as well).

key_terms.الْمَسْجِد: The mosque, a place of worship
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family (SAWW)
key_terms.فَصَلِّ: So send blessings (imperative form of Salawat)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication or action when entering and leaving the mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual protocol of framing one's visit to the mosque with Salawat, establishing a continuous connection with the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) throughout the act of worship. In Shia tradition, this practice underscores the belief that the Prophet's intercession and presence are integral to the sanctity of the mosque, transforming the physical entry and exit into moments of spiritual elevation and gratitude.
